slides.title: ADSS or lashed cable?
slides.sub: Choosing the right aerial fiber design

slides.title: Same pole line, two very different cables.
slides.body: One hangs from a steel strand. The other holds itself up.

slides.title: ADSS has no metal
slides.body: All-dielectric self-supporting. Aramid yarn carries the span tension, so no bonding or grounding is needed.

slides.title: It can sit near power
slides.body: With a track-resistant jacket, ADSS can go in the supply space, close to energised conductors.

slides.title: Lashed rewards growth
slides.body: Steel strand carries the load. Adding a cable later is easy: overlash it onto the existing bundle.

slides.title: Save this for your next aerial design

caption:
From the sidewalk, ADSS and lashed fiber look almost the same. On the design sheet they are very different.

ADSS carries its own weight on aramid yarn and has no metal to ground. Lashed cable hangs on a steel strand and makes adding cables easy. Swipe for the side-by-side.
